summary: OpenAI is rolling out an upgraded memory synthesis system ("dreaming") for ChatGPT that automatically curates and updates user memories in the background, launching to Plus/Pro users in the US now and to Free users and more countries in the coming weeks after a roughly 5x reduction in the compute needed to serve it.

mechanisms.reason: The document states a concrete 5x reduction in compute required to serve the memory-synthesis feature, a stated efficiency figure, though scoped to one feature rather than model inference broadly.
mechanisms.quote: Recent improvements reduced the compute required to serve dreaming to Free users by approximately 5x, making it possible to begin rolling out dreaming to Free users over the coming weeks and to increase memory capacity for Plus and Pro users.

mechanisms.reason: Expanding a background memory-synthesis process to Free-tier users across ChatGPT's user base increases the aggregate volume of model calls being run.
mechanisms.quote: we observe when memory is applied to the hundreds of millions of users and multi-year time horizons in ChatGPT

mechanisms.reason: The rollout explicitly increases the amount of memory state retained per user for Plus and Pro accounts.
mechanisms.quote: increase memory capacity for Plus and Pro users

practices.reason: A 5x compute reduction for serving this feature is reported but tied entirely to OpenAI's own infrastructure and not described as a reproducible recipe.
practices.quote: Recent improvements reduced the compute required to serve dreaming to Free users by approximately 5x

practices.reason: The document describes an internal evaluation methodology for memory quality (recall, preference-following, staying current over time) but it is the lab's own process, not a transferable instrument.
practices.quote: We can construct an eval from examples that resemble this where the model is asked to respond to a prompt that requires it to recall factual information about the user.
